items.title: After a V-admissible blowing up a proper morphism becomes an isomorphism over a neighbourhood of the closure of a closed subset where it was already one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a proper morphism f : X -> Y of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, a quasi-compact open V of Y with preimage U, and a closed subset T of V over a neighbourhood of which f|_U is an isomorphism, the lemma produces a V-admissible blowing up Y' -> Y such that the strict transform f' : X' -> Y' is an isomorphism over a neighbourhood of the closure of T in Y' (statement lines 9607-9617). The proof isolates the obstruction as the closed subset T' where f|_U fails to be an isomorphism, disjoint from T, and then separates the two by constructible approximations: since V is spectral one finds constructible closed T_c containing T and T'_c containing T' with empty intersection, explicitly via quasi-compact opens (proof lines 9620-9629). A disjoint-locally-closed separation lemma lets one blow up so that the two closures become disjoint, after which the complement Y_0 of the closure of T'_c carries a V_0-admissible blowing up making the strict transform an isomorphism by the Zariski-after-blowup lemma, and an extension result for admissible blowups lifts that local solution back to a V-admissible blowing up of Y (proof lines 9630-9643). Separating the obstruction from T by constructible approximations and then lifting the local solution is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
